newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: U.N. food convoys, refugees enter Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: U.N. food convoys, refugees enter Afghanistan.

text.p: U.N. food convoys and busloads of Afghan refugees have begun entering Afghanistan with tensions along the border easing after last week's Islamic Taleban takeover, officials based in Pakistan said on Tuesday.

Code Cisse, head of the local office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, told Reuters 110 minibuses loaded with recent refugees had returned to Afghanistan on Monday and Tuesday after bombing ceased around the town of Jalalabad.

"This is spontaneous, it is not organised. Refugees are already going back and we expect others to leave soon," he said, adding the refugees were among some 10,000 recent arrivals since the fall of Jalalabad in late September.
Forces loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani had bombed the city, 70 km (40 miles) from the Pakistan border, since Taleban forces overran the town several weeks ago.
The bombing ended after the Islamic militia took the capital Kabul and the nearby Bagram air base last week.

Some 25 U.N. trucks loaded with food, medical equipment and other supplies crossed the border to Kabul after Pakistani officials opened the border late on Monday, local district chief Javed Iqbal said by telephone on Tuesday.
It was the first time in months such supplies had got through, officials said.
The International Committee of the Red Cross, which assisted the effort, said it was planning further trips but did not give details.
